pr_title: Send task logs from KubeExecutor tasks to pod stdout too
pr_body:
This is needed so that when the KubeExecutor is asked to get logs for a
running pod they show up in the pod.

This changes the `airflow.sdk.execution_time.execute_workload` entrypoint to
a. produce all logs as JSON, and
b. ask the SDK to send all output log messages to the top level logger to, so
   they appear on stdout.

In order to make the output a bit nicer this also tidies up/removes some of
the logging from dispose_orm so that it doesn't "pollute" the logs (this was
required as due to the current hack we have to upload remote logs, we ended up
alling dispose_orm at the end and that _wasn't_ JSON formatted).

Closes #46894

issue_context.title: Write task logs to stdout for tasks run with KubernetesExecutor
issue_context.body:
### Body

We need to write the task logs from a task also to the stdout of the worker pods so that it can be streamed by the log reader and that can be shown to the UI as well. 

Currently for non task sdk, it works by double logging -- both to the stdout as well as to the file. We should try and do the same for task sdk too. We’d have to write it ourselves, possibly make those log fn take multiple loggers to write too

### Committer

- [x] I acknowledge that I am a maintainer/committer of the Apache Airflow project.

review_comments:
it seems odd that `self.log` would not go to stdout but `log` would go to stdout.  so if i use  the global `log`, it will not go to task logs? 

shouldn't it be more idiot proof than that, in the sense that, whichever log you a re using, it would go to both?

if `log` is a special "stdout only" logger, it should probably be named specially to reflect that

`self.log` is the process specific logger, which is configured to write to the file.

`log` is the top level module scoped generic logger.

Would renaming `self.log` to `self.process_log`  or `process_logger` help do you think?
